title: S. Korea, Japan Have Best Paternity Leave Pay — Study
paragraphs: Paternity leave gives new fathers time to bond with their children, and may also help decrease gender inequality by making it easier for parents to share the work of looking after a little one and their home.
A study by British payroll company Moorepay has found that South Korea has the highest-value statutory paid paternity leave in the world, followed by Japan.
For its study, Moorepay looked at the cash value of paternity leave around the world, converting it all into "international dollars."

International dollars are a hypothetical currency used in economic research to understand purchasing power. While based on US dollars, they are not a direct conversion, as they take cost of living into account.

For example, a cup of coffee might cost $5 in the US, but cost the equivalent of $1 in India. So just converting your Indian rupee would not buy you as much in the US, and at the same time, you don't need as many US dollars to buy things in India.
So to better understand purchasing power around the world, one international dollar buys the same goods and services that $1 would in the US, wherever it is spent.

Fathers in South Korea can be paid up to 36 million won during their paternity leave, which according to the study is worth 42,797 international dollars — more than any other country. Japan offers the second-most-valuable pay for paternity leave, worth the equivalent of around 27,500 international dollars.
The third best is Sweden, where new fathers can be paid around 25,000 international dollars.
However, the lowest statutory paternity leave pay is shared by 51 countries, including the US, Russia and Serbia — all of which simply do not offer it.
South Korea also gives the longest paid paternity leave, at 82 weeks, again followed by Japan, which gives 48 weeks. Next is Hungary, which gives just over 42 weeks.
